as_told.title: Ruth Paine takes in Lee Harvey Oswald

plain: In 1963 a woman named Ruth Paine took Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy, and his wife Marina Oswald into her house in Texas. The writer Peter Levenda, billed on the show as a historian of the CIA, tells it without naming a source, and simply says the Oswalds were living with Ruth Paine in that house. Michels brings it up too, while tracing family ties among people he links to the CIA. He says he thinks Ruth Paine was the daughter of a woman he is discussing, and that she is the one who took in Oswald. Both tell it because they see the Oswalds' hosts as part of a wider web of connections behind the Kennedy killing.
